PullRequest.Title: Add setup-feed script for npm registry configuration
PullRequest.Body: Introduce a script to configure npm registry settings for Azure Artifacts, facilitating easier package management. Include a reauthentication command for the feed. Test by running the `setup-feed` script to ensure proper registry setup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Developer explicitly runs `npm run setup-feed` to configure the private npm registry.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command cannot finish until the credential-provider package installation completes and then `npm config set registry` writes configuration; none of this runs during application startup, build, install, rendering, or other implicit workflows.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launches npm to globally install one named credential-provider package, then launches npm config to set one registry value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two top-level subprocesses per explicit invocation; installation transitively resolves the single package's dependency graph, not a repository-sized collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No setup-feed script or associated subprocesses existed; developers had to perform equivalent setup manually.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both subprocesses are on the explicit setup command's critical path, with the config write beginning only after installation succeeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolves and downloads `@microsoft/artifacts-npm-credprovider` and any dependencies from the specified Azure Artifacts registry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One package-install transaction per explicit invocation, with requests bounded by that package's dependency graph and npm cache state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The repository exposed no command that initiated this install, although equivalent manual installation necessarily incurred the same network work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold-cache registry resolution/download blocks setup; warm npm caches can reduce transferred bytes and latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: package.json:101 `npm install --global` and `npm config set registry`
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Writes the global package installation and npm registry configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One global install update and one config update per explicit invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No repository script performed these writes; equivalent manual setup performed them outside this command.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The writes complete before the setup command exits.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A single named package and its bounded dependency graph per user invocation; no workspace files, repositories, rows, messages, or history control multiplicity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two commands are serialized by `&&`; npm may internally parallelize bounded dependency downloads, but the diff adds no loop, fan-out, queue, or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: npm's normal package cache can make repeated installs warmer, but the script intentionally invokes installation each time and adds no custom cache, cache key, negative cache, or request coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the command adds sequential network/filesystem setup work only when explicitly invoked; the changed package.json script has no implicit lifecycle hook.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact package dependency count, cache-hit rate, registry latency, and global installation duration are not established, but invocation is manual and bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the expensive work is the requested, opt-in setup operation, is bounded to one package installation, and does not move onto a hot product path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Developer explicitly runs `npm run reauth-feed` to force credential refresh.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The npm wrapper and credential-provider command must finish authentication before this explicit command completes; it is not wired into installs, startup, build, or application interaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launches `artifacts-npm-credprovider --force` through the npm script runner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No repository reauthentication script existed; developers had to invoke the credential provider directly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Credential refresh is the entire explicit reauthentication command's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The credential provider may contact the configured authentication/feed service to force credential refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One credential-refresh flow per explicit invocation, with no collection-driven multiplicity visible in the changed code.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The repository did not initiate this flow; equivalent direct reauthentication incurred the same boundary outside the script.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Any authentication/network interaction blocks completion of the manually requested reauthentication.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicit refresh request per command invocation; no collection or persistent history increases work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One credential-provider invocation with no changed loop, batching, fan-out, limiter, or concurrent scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: `--force` intentionally bypasses reuse of an existing credential for this manually requested refresh; no changed automatic caller repeatedly defeats the credential cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that only one manually triggered provider process is added; possible internal network work is bounded by a single refresh flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The provider's internal request count and authentication latency are not visible in the repository, but the changed invocation count and opt-in reachability are clear.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: forced refresh is explicit command semantics rather than newly repeated or hot-path work.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file, one-hunk diff. The PR adds two manually invoked npm scripts with bounded sequential subprocess/network/filesystem work and no integration into lifecycle hooks or product runtime paths. No actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
